'''600''' ('''six hundred''') is the [[natural number]] following 599 and preceding 601.
{{TOC limit|3}}

==Mathematical properties==
Six hundred is a [[composite number]], an [[abundant number]], a [[pronic number]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite OEIS|A002378|Oblong (or promic, pronic, or heteromecic) numbers}}</ref> a [[Harshad number]] and a [[largely composite number]].<ref name="OEIS-A067128">{{Cite OEIS|A067128|Ramanujan's largely composite numbers}}</ref>

==Credit==
In the United States, a [[credit score]] of 600 or below is considered poor, limiting available credit at a normal interest rate

==Integers from 601 to 699==

===600s===

==== 601 ====
601 is a prime number and a [[centered pentagonal number]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite OEIS|A005891|Centered pentagonal numbers}}</ref>
==== 602 ====
602 = 2 × 7 × 43. It is a [[nontotient]]. There are 602 cubes of edge length 1 required to make a hollow cube of edge length 11<ref>{{Cite web |title=A005897 - OEIS |url=https://oeis.org/A005897 |access-date=2026-06-14 |website=oeis.org}}</ref>
==== 603 ====
603 = 3<sup>2</sup> × 67. It is a [[Harshad number]] and a Riordan number.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A005043 - OEIS |url=https://oeis.org/A005043 |access-date=2026-06-14 |website=oeis.org}}</ref>

==== 604 ====
604 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 151. It is a [[nontotient]] and the totient sum for first 44 integers.

==== 605 ====
605 = 5 × 11<sup>2</sup>. It is a [[Harshad number]] and the sum of the nontriangular numbers between the two successive [[Triangular number|triangular numbers]] 55 and 66.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A006002 - OEIS |url=https://oeis.org/A006002 |access-date=2026-06-14 |website=oeis.org}}</ref> There are 605 non-isomorphic set-systems of weight 9.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A283877 - OEIS |url=https://oeis.org/A283877 |access-date=2026-06-14 |website=oeis.org}}</ref>

==== 606 ====
606 = 2 × 3 × 101. It is a [[sphenic number]], an admirable number<ref name=":11">{{Cite web |title=A111592 - OEIS |url=https://oeis.org/A111592 |access-date=2026-06-14 |website=oeis.org}}</ref> and the sum of six consecutive primes (89 + 97 + 101 + 103 + 107 + 109).

606 is one of the numbers associated with Christ - ΧϚʹ - see the [[Greek numerals]] [[Isopsephy]] and the reason why other numbers siblings with this one are Beast's numbers.

==== 607 ====
607 is a prime number, a [[balanced prime]],<ref name=":2">{{Cite OEIS|A006562|Balanced primes}}</ref> a [[Mersenne prime]] exponent, the sum of three consecutive primes (197 + 199 + 211), a zero of [[Mertens function]] and a strictly non-palindromic number<ref name=":3">{{Cite OEIS|A016038|Strictly non-palindromic numbers}}</ref>

==== 608 ====
608 = 2<sup>5</sup> × 19. It is a [[nontotient]], a [[happy number]], and a zero of the [[Mertens function]]. There are 608 regions formed by drawing the line segments connecting any two of the perimeter points of a 3 times 4 grid of squares<ref name="OEIS452">{{Cite OEIS|A331452|2=Triangle read by rows: T(n,m) (n >= m >= 1) = number of regions (or cells) formed by drawing the line segments connecting any two of the 2*(m+n) perimeter points of an m X n grid of squares}}</ref>

==== 609 ====
609 = 3 × 7 × 29. It is a [[sphenic number]] and a [[strobogrammatic number]].<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A000787|Strobogrammatic numbers}}</ref>

===610s===

==== 610 ====
{{Main|610 (number)}}
610 =2 × 5 × 61. It is a [[deficient number]], a [[Markov number]], a [[sphenic number]], and a member of the [[Fibonacci sequence]].

==== 611 ====
611 = 13 × 47. It is the sum of the three standard board sizes in Go (9<sup>2</sup> + 13<sup>2</sup> + 19<sup>2</sup>).

The 611th [[Tribonacci|tribonacci number]] is prime.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A232543 - OEIS |url=https://oeis.org/A232543 |access-date=2026-06-14 |website=oeis.org}}</ref>

==== 612 ====
612 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 3<sup>2</sup> × 17. It is a [[Harshad number]], an [[untouchable number]], and a Zuckerman number {{OEIS|id=A007602}}.

==== 613 ====
{{Main|613 (number)}}
==== 614 ====
614 = 2 × 307. It is a [[nontotient]] and a [[Knödel number|2-Knödel number]].

According to Rabbi [[Emil Fackenheim]], the number of Commandments in Judaism should be 614 rather than the traditional 613.

==== 615 ====
615 = 3 × 5 × 41. It is a [[sphenic number]].

==== 616 ====
{{Main|616 (number)}}
616 = 2<sup>3</sup> × 7 × 11. It is a [[Padovan sequence|Padovan number]] and a balanced number.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A020492|Balanced numbers: numbers k such that phi(k) (A000010) divides sigma(k) (A000203)}}</ref>

616 is an alternative value for the [[Number of the Beast (numerology)|Number of the Beast]] (more commonly accepted to be [[666 (number)|666]])

==== 617 ====
617 is a prime number, a [[Chen prime]], an [[Eisenstein prime]] with no imaginary part, a [[super-prime]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=A006450 - OEIS |url=https://oeis.org/A006450 |access-date=2026-06-14 |website=oeis.org}}</ref> an index of prime Lucas number,<ref name="ReferenceC">{{cite OEIS|A001606|Indices of prime Lucas numbers}}</ref> and the sum of five consecutive primes (109 + 113 + 127 + 131 + 137).

There are 617 compositions of 17 into distinct parts.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A032020|Number of compositions (ordered partitions) of n into distinct parts|access-date=2022-05-24}}</ref>

==== 618 ====
618 = 2 × 3 × 103. It is a [[sphenic number]] and an admirable number.<ref name=":11" />

==== 619 ====
619 is a prime number, a [[strobogrammatic prime]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A007597|Strobogrammatic primes}}</ref> and an [[alternating factorial]].<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A005165|Alternating factorials}}</ref>

===620s===

==== 620 ====
620 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 5 × 31. It is the sum of four consecutive primes (149 + 151 + 157 + 163) and the sum of eight consecutive primes (61 + 67 + 71 + 73 + 79 + 83 + 89 + 97).

The sum of the first 620 primes is itself prime.<ref>{{oeis|A013916}}</ref>

==== 621 ====
621 = 3<sup>3</sup> × 23. It is a Harshad number, and it is the discriminant of a totally real cubic field.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A006832|Discriminants of totally real cubic fields}}</ref>
==== 622 ====
622 = 2 × 311. It isa [[nontotient]] and a fine number {{OEIS|A000957}}.
==== 623 ====
623 = 7 × 89. There are 623 partitions of 23 into an even number of parts.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A027187|Number of partitions of n into an even number of parts}}</ref>
==== 624 ====
624 = 2<sup>4</sup> × 3 × 13. It is a Harshad number, a Zuckerman number and the sum of a twin prime pair (311 + 313).

624=[[Jordan's totient function|J<sub>4</sub>(5)]].<ref>{{cite OEIS|A059377|Jordan function J_4(n)}}</ref> 

==== 625 ====
625 = 25<sup>2</sup> = 5<sup>4</sup> It is a [[centered octagonal number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A016754|2=Odd squares: a(n) = (2n+1)^2. Also centered octagonal numbers}}</ref> a 1-[[automorphic number]], a [[Friedman number]] because 625 = 5<sup>6&minus;2</sup>,<ref name=":4">{{Cite OEIS|A036057|Friedman numbers}}</ref> the sum of seven consecutive primes (73 + 79 + 83 + 89 + 97 + 101 + 103). 

It is  one of the two three-digit numbers that when squared or raised to a higher power that end in the same three digits, the other being [[300_(number)#376|376]].

==== 626 ====
626 = 2 × 313. It is a [[nontotient]] and a [[Knödel number|2-Knödel number]],

* [[Stitch (Lilo & Stitch)|Stitch]]'s experiment number

==== 627 ====
627 = 3 × 11 × 19. It is a sphenic number and a [[Smith number]]<ref name=":5">{{Cite OEIS|A006753|Smith numbers}}</ref> There are 627 [[integer partition]]s of 20. <ref>{{Cite OEIS|A000041|2=a(n) = number of partitions of n}}</ref>

==== 628 ====
628 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 157. It is a [[nontotient]] and the totient sum for first 45 integers.
==== 629 ====
629 = 17 × 37. It is a [[highly cototient number]]<ref name=":6">{{Cite OEIS|A100827|Highly cototient numbers}}</ref> and a [[Harshad number]]. There are 629 diagonals in a 37-gon.<ref name="ReferenceA">{{cite OEIS|A000096|2=a(n) = n*(n+3)/2}}</ref>
===630s===

==== 630 ====
630 = 2 × 3<sup>2</sup> × 5 × 7. It is a [[hexagonal number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A000384|Hexagonal numbers}}</ref> a [[sparsely totient number]],<ref name=":7">{{Cite OEIS|A036913|Sparsely totient numbers}}</ref> a Harshad number, a balanced number,<ref>{{cite OEIS|A020492|Balanced numbers: numbers k such that phi(k) (A000010) divides sigma(k) (A000203)}}</ref> a [[largely composite number]],<ref name="OEIS-A067128">{{Cite OEIS|A067128|Ramanujan's largely composite numbers}}</ref> the 35th [[triangular number]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=A000217 - OEIS |url=https://oeis.org/A000217 |access-date=2024-11-29 |website=oeis.org}}</ref> and the sum of six consecutive primes (97 + 101 + 103 + 107 + 109 + 113).
==== 631 ====
631 is a prime number, a [[Cuban prime]], a [[Lucky prime]] a Chen prime, a [[centered triangular number]],<ref name=":8">{{Cite OEIS|A005448|Centered triangular numbers}}</ref> a [[centered hexagonal number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A003215|Hex (or centered hexagonal) numbers}}</ref> and a lazy caterer number {{OEIS|id=A000124}}.

==== 632 ====
632 = 2<sup>3</sup> × 79. It is a [[refactorable number]]. There are 632 13-bead necklaces with 2 colors<ref>{{cite OEIS|A000031|Number of n-bead necklaces with 2 colors when turning over is not allowed; also number of output sequences from a simple n-stage cycling shift register; also number of binary irreducible polynomials whose degree divides n}}</ref>
==== 633 ====
633 = 3 × 211. It is a [[Blum integer]] and the sum of three consecutive primes (199 + 211 + 223).

==== 634 ====
634 = 2 × 317. It is a [[nontotient]] and a Smith number.<ref name=":5" />

==== 635 ====
635 = 5 × 127. It is a zero of the [[Mertens function]] and the sum of nine consecutive primes (53 + 59 + 61 + 67 + 71 + 73 + 79 + 83 + 89).

There are 635 [[Composition (combinatorics)|compositions]] of 13 into pairwise relatively prime parts.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A101268|Number of compositions of n into pairwise relatively prime parts|access-date=2022-05-31}}</ref>
{{sfrac|635|504}} ≈ [[∛2]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Continued Fractions and Characteristic Recurrences|url=https://www.mathpages.com/home/kmath434.htm|website=Math Pages}}</ref>

==== 636 ====
636 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 3 × 53. It is a [[Smith number]],<ref name=":5" /> a zero of the [[Mertens function]], and the sum of ten consecutive primes (43 + 47 + 53 + 59 + 61 + 67 + 71 + 73 + 79 + 83).

==== 637 ====
637 = 7<sup>2</sup> × 13. It is a [[decagonal number]]<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A001107|10-gonal (or decagonal) numbers}}</ref> and a zero of the [[Mertens function]].

==== 638 ====
638 = 2 × 11 × 29. It is a sphenic number, a [[nontotient]], a [[centered heptagonal number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A069099|Centered heptagonal numbers}}</ref> and the sum of four consecutive primes (151 + 157 + 163 + 167).
==== 639 ====
639 = 3<sup>2</sup> × 71. It is the sum of the first twenty primes.
===640===

==== 640 ====
640 = 2<sup>7</sup> × 5. It is a [[Harshad number]], a [[refactorable number]], and a hexadecagonal number<ref>{{cite OEIS|A051868|2=16-gonal (or hexadecagonal) numbers: a(n) = n*(7*n-6)}}</ref>

There are 640 1's in all partitions of 24 into odd parts,<ref>{{cite OEIS|A036469|Partial sums of A000009 (partitions into distinct parts)}}</ref> 
There are 640 acres in a square mile.

==== 641 ====
641 is a prime number, a [[Sophie Germain prime]],<ref name=":9">{{Cite OEIS|A005384|Sophie Germain primes}}</ref> a Chen prime, an Eisenstein prime with no imaginary part and a [[Proth prime]]. It is a factor of [[4294967297 (number)|4294967297]], the smallest nonprime [[Fermat number]].

==== 642 ====
642 = 2 × 3 × 107. It is a [[sphenic number]] and an admirable number.<ref name=":11" />

642= 1<sup>4</sup> + 2<sup>4</sup> + 5<sup>4</sup>,<ref>{{cite OEIS|A074501|2=a(n) = 1^n + 2^n + 5^n|access-date=2022-05-31}}</ref> making 642 a counterexample of  

==== 643 ====
643 is a [[prime number]].
==== 644 ====
644 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 7 × 23. It is a [[nontotient]], a [[Perrin number]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A001608|title=Sloane's A001608 : Perrin sequence|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> a Harshad number, an admirable number<ref name=":11" /> and a common [[umask]].

==== 645 ====
645 = 3 × 5 × 43. It is a [[sphenic number]], an [[octagonal number]], a Smith number,<ref name=":5" /> a Harshad number and a [[Fermat pseudoprime]] to base 2.<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A001567|Fermat pseudoprimes to base 2}}</ref>

==== 646 ====
646 = 2 × 17 × 19. It is a sphenic number

There are 646 permutations of length 7 without rising or falling successions.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A002464|Hertzsprung's problem: ways to arrange n non-attacking kings on an n X n board, with 1 in each row and column. Also number of permutations of length n without rising or falling successions}}</ref> 
==== 647 ====
647 is a Chen prime, an Eisenstein prime with no imaginary part, and the sum of five consecutive primes (113 + 127 + 131 + 137 + 139).

3<sup>647</sup> - 2<sup>647</sup> is prime<ref>{{cite OEIS|A057468|Numbers k such that 3^k - 2^k is prime}}</ref>

==== 648 ====
648 = 2<sup>3</sup> × 3<sup>4</sup>. It is a [[Harshad number]] and an [[Achilles number]].
==== 649 ====
649 = 11 × 59. It is a [[Blum integer]].
===650s===

==== 650 ====
650 = 2 × 5<sup>2</sup> × 13. It is a [[primitive abundant number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A071395|Primitive abundant numbers}}</ref> a [[square pyramidal number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A000330|Square pyramidal numbers}}</ref> a pronic number,<ref name=":0" /> a [[nontotient]] an admirable number,<ref name=":11" /> and the [[Totient summatory function|totient sum]] for first 46 integers.
==== 651 ====
651 = 3 × 7 × 31. It is a sphenic number, a [[pentagonal number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A000326|Pentagonal numbers}}</ref> and a [[nonagonal number]].<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A001106|9-gonal (or enneagonal or nonagonal) numbers}}</ref>
==== 652 ====
652 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 163. It is the maximal number of regions by drawing 26 circles<ref>{{cite OEIS|A014206|2=a(n) = n^2 + n + 2}}</ref>
==== 653 ====
653 is a prime number, a Sophie Germain prime,<ref name=":9" /> a balanced prime,<ref name=":2" /> a Chen prime, and an Eisenstein prime with no imaginary part.
==== 654 ====
654 = 2 × 3 × 109. It is a sphenic number, a [[nontotient]], a Smith number,<ref name=":5" /> and an admirable number<ref name=":11" />
==== 655 ====
655 = 5 × 131. There are 655 toothpicks after 20 stages in a three-dimensional grid.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A160160|Toothpick sequence in the three-dimensional grid}}</ref>
==== 656 ====
656 = 2<sup>4</sup> × 41 = <math>\lfloor \frac{3^{16}}{2^{16}} \rfloor</math>,<ref>{{cite OEIS|A002379|2=a(n) = floor(3^n / 2^n)}}</ref> 

In [[Judaism]], [[Jerusalem]] is mentioned in the [[Hebrew Bible]] and the [[Old Testament]] a total of 656 times.

==== 657 ====
657 = 3<sup>2</sup> × 73. It is the largest known number not of the form ''a''<sup>2</sup>+''s'' with ''s'' a [[semiprime]]

==== 658 ====
658 = 2 × 7 × 47. It is a [[sphenic number]] and an [[untouchable number]].
==== 659 ====
659 is a prime number, a Sophie Germain prime,<ref name=":9" /> a Chen prime an Eisenstein prime with no imaginary part, strictly non-palindromic number,<ref name=":3" /> highly cototient number,<ref name=":6" /> and the sum of seven consecutive primes (79 + 83 + 89 + 97 + 101 + 103 + 107).

Mertens function sets a new low of &minus;10 at 659 which stands until 661.

===660s===

==== 660 ====
660 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 3 × 5 × 11. It is a sparsely totient number,<ref name=":7" /> a [[Harshad number]], and a [[largely composite number]].<ref name="OEIS-A067128" /> It is the sum of four consecutive primes (157 + 163 + 167 + 173), the sum of six consecutive primes (101 + 103 + 107 + 109 + 113 + 127), and the sum of eight consecutive primes (67 + 71 + 73 + 79 + 83 + 89 + 97 + 101). It is the sum of 11th row when writing the natural numbers as a triangle.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A027480|2=a(n) = n*(n+1)*(n+2)/2}}</ref>

==== 661 ====
661 is:

* a prime number

*the sum of three consecutive primes (211 + 223 + 227)
*a [[Pentagram]] number of the form <math>5n^{2}-5n+1</math> 
*a [[Hexagram]] number of the form <math>6n^{2}-6n+1</math> i.e. a [[star number]]
Mertens function sets new low of &minus;11 at 661 which stands until 665.

==== 662 ====
662 = 2 × 331. It is a [[nontotient]] and a member of [[Mian–Chowla sequence]].<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A005282|Mian-Chowla sequence}}</ref>
==== 663 ====
663 = 3 × 13 × 17. It is a [[sphenic number]] and a Smith number.<ref name=":5" />
==== 664 ====
664 = 2<sup>3</sup> × 83. It is a [[refactorable number]].

There are 664 knapsack partitions of 33.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A108917|Number of knapsack partitions of n}}</ref>
==== 665 ====
665 = 5 × 7 × 19. It is a [[sphenic number]].

There are 665 diagonals in a 38-gon.<ref name="ReferenceA" />
Mertens function sets new low of &minus;12 at 665 which stands until 1105.

==== 666 ====
{{Main|666 (number)}}
==== 667 ====
667 = 23 × 29. It is a [[Lazy caterer's sequence|lazy caterer number]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=A000124 - OEIS |url=https://oeis.org/A000124 |access-date=2026-07-02 |website=oeis.org}}</ref>
==== 668 ====
668 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 167. It is a [[nontotient]].
==== 669 ====
669 = 3 × 223. It is a [[Blum integer]].
===670s===

==== 670 ====
670 = 2 × 5 × 67. It is a sphenic number, an [[octahedral number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A005900|Octahedral numbers}}</ref> and a [[nontotient]].
==== 671 ====
671 = 11 × 61.

The [[magic constant]] of ''n''×''n'' normal [[magic square]] and [[Eight queens puzzle|''n''-queens problem]] for&nbsp;''n''&nbsp;=&nbsp;11 is 671.

==== 672 ====
672 = 2<sup>5</sup> × 3 × 7. It is a [[harmonic divisor number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A001599|Harmonic or Ore numbers}}</ref> a Zuckerman number, an admirable number,<ref name=":11" /> a [[largely composite number]],<ref name="OEIS-A067128">{{Cite OEIS|A067128|Ramanujan's largely composite numbers}}</ref> and a [[triperfect number]].
==== 673 ====
673 is a prime number, a lucky prime, and a Proth prime.<ref name=":10">{{Cite OEIS|A080076|Proth primes}}</ref>
==== 674 ====
674 = 2 × 337. It is a [[nontotient]] and a [[Knödel number|2-Knödel number]].
==== 675 ====
675 = 3<sup>3</sup> × 5<sup>2</sup>. It is an [[Achilles number]].

==== 676 ====
676 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 13<sup>2</sup> = 26<sup>2</sup>. It is a palindromic square.

==== 677 ====
677 is a prime number, a Chen prime, and an Eisenstein prime with no imaginary part.

There are 677 non-isomorphic self-dual multiset partitions of weight 10.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A316983|Number of non-isomorphic self-dual multiset partitions of weight n}}</ref>

==== 678 ====
678 = 2 × 3 × 113. It is a sphenic number, a [[nontotient]], and an admirable number.<ref name=":11" />

There are 678 surface points of an octahedron with side length 13.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A005899|Number of points on surface of octahedron with side n|access-date=2022-05-31}}</ref> 

==== 679 ====
679 = 7 × 97. It is the sum of three consecutive primes (223 + 227 + 229) and the sum of nine consecutive primes (59 + 61 + 67 + 71 + 73 + 79 + 83 + 89 + 97). It is the smallest number of multiplicative persistence 5.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A003001|Smallest number of multiplicative persistence n|access-date=2022-05-31}}</ref>
===680s===

==== 680 ====
680 = 2<sup>3</sup> × 5 × 17. It is a [[tetrahedral number]]<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A000292|Tetrahedral numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> and a [[nontotient]].
==== 681 ====
681 = 3 × 227. It is a centered pentagonal number.<ref name=":1" />
==== 682 ====
682 = 2 × 11 × 31. It is a sphenic number, the sum of four consecutive primes (163 + 167 + 173 + 179), and the sum of ten consecutive primes (47 + 53 + 59 + 61 + 67 + 71 + 73 + 79 + 83 + 89).

Solving the Norwegian puzzle strikketoy<ref>{{cite OEIS|A000975|Lichtenberg sequence|access-date=2022-05-31}}</ref> requires 682 moves.

==== 683 ====
683 is a prime number, a Sophie Germain prime,<ref name=":9" /> a Chen prime, an Eisenstein prime with no imaginary part, a [[Wagstaff prime]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A000979|Wagstaff primes|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> and the sum of five consecutive primes (127 + 131 + 137 + 139 + 149).
==== 684 ====
684 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 3<sup>2</sup> × 19. It is a Harshad number.

There are 684 graphical forest partitions of 32.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A000070|2=a(n) = Sum_{k=0..n} p(k) where p(k) = number of partitions of k (A000041)|access-date=2022-05-31}}</ref>

==== 685 ====
685 = 5 × 137 It is a centered square number.<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A001844|Centered square numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>
==== 686 ====
686 = 2 × 7<sup>3</sup>.It is a [[nontotient]]. There are 686 multigraphs on infinite set of nodes with 7 edges.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A050535|Number of multigraphs on infinite set of nodes with n edges|access-date=2022-05-31}}</ref>

==== 687 ====
687 = 3 × 229. It is a [[Knödel number|D-number]].<ref name="ReferenceB">{{cite OEIS|A033553|2=3-Knödel numbers or D-numbers: numbers n > 3 such that n divides k^(n-2)-k for all k with gcd(k, n) = 1|access-date=2022-05-31}}</ref> 
[[Mars]] takes 687 days to orbit around the sun.

==== 688 ====
688 = 2<sup>4</sup> × 43. It is a 2-[[automorphic number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A030984|2-automorphic numbers|access-date=2021-09-01}}</ref> and a [[Friedman number]] since 688 = 8 × 86.<ref name=":4" />

==== 689 ====
689 = 13 × 53. It is a [[Strobogrammatic number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A000787|Strobogrammatic numbers}}</ref> the sum of three consecutive primes (227 + 229 + 233), and the sum of seven consecutive primes (83 + 89 + 97 + 101 + 103 + 107 + 109).

===690s===

==== 690 ====
690 = 2 × 3 × 5 × 23. It is a sparsely totient number,<ref name=":7" /> a Smith number,<ref name=":5" /> a Harshad number, and the sum of six consecutive primes (103 + 107 + 109 + 113 + 127 + 131).
==== 691 ====
691 is a prime number.

[[Ramanujan's tau function]] τ and the [[divisor function]] σ<sub>11</sub> are related by the congruence τ(''n'') ≡ σ<sub>11</sub>(''n'') (mod 691). 

Negative 691 is the numerator of the [[Bernoulli number]] ''B''<sub>12</sub> = -691/2730. In number theory, 691 is a "marker" (similar to the radioactive markers in biology): whenever it appears in a computation, it is a sign that Bernoulli numbers are involved.

==== 692 ====
692 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 173. There are 692 partitions of 48 into powers of 2.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A000123|Number of binary partitions: number of partitions of 2n into powers of 2|access-date=2022-05-31}}</ref>
==== 693 ====
693 = 3<sup>2</sup> × 7 × 11.

693 appears as the first three digits after the decimal point in the decimal form for the [[natural logarithm of 2]]. To 10 digits, this number is 0.'''693'''1471805.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein|first=Eric W.|title=Natural Logarithm of 2|url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/NaturalLogarithmof2.html|access-date=2026-07-29|website=mathworld.wolfram.com|language=en}}</ref> As a result, if an event has a constant [[probability]] of 0.1% of occurring, 693 is the smallest number of trials that must be performed for there to be at least a 50% chance that the event occurs at least once. More generally, for any probability p, the probability that the event occurs at least once in a sample of n items, assuming the items are independent, is given by the following formula:{{Citation needed|date=July 2026}}

1 − (1 − p)<sup>n</sup>

For p = 10<sup>−3</sup> = 0.001, plugging in n = 692 gives, to four decimal places, 0.4996, while n = 693 yields 0.5001.{{Citation needed|date=July 2026}}

693 is a palindrome in [[Binary number|binary]] in bases [[Base32|32]], [[Base 62|62]], 76, 98, 230, and 692.{{Citation needed|date=July 2026}}

==== 694 ====
694 = 2 × 347. It is a centered triangular number,<ref name=":8" /> a [[nontotient]], and the smallest pandigital number in base 5.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A049363|2=a(1) = 1; for n > 1, smallest digitally balanced number in base n}}</ref>

==== 695 ====
695 = 5 × 139. 

695!! + 2 is prime.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A076185|Numbers n such that n!! + 2 is prime|access-date=2022-05-31}}</ref>

==== 696 ====
696 = 2<sup>3</sup> × 3 × 29. It is the totient sum for first 47 integers, the sum of a twin prime pair (347 + 349), and the sum of eight consecutive primes (71 + 73 + 79 + 83 + 89 + 97 + 101 + 103). There are 696 trails of length 9 on honeycomb lattice.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A006851|Trails of length n on honeycomb lattice|access-date=2022-05-18}}</ref>

==== 697 ====
697 = 17 × 41. It is a [[cake number]].The US state of Colorado has 697 sides.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bigthink.com/strange-maps/colorado-is-not-a-rectangle|title=Colorado is a rectangle? Think again|date=23 January 2023 }}</ref>

==== 698 ====
698 = 2 × 349. It is a [[nontotient]] and the sum of squares of two primes.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A045636|Numbers of the form p^2 + q^2, with p and q primes}}</ref>

==== 699 ====
699 = 3 × 233. It is a [[Knödel number|D-number]].<ref name="ReferenceB" />
